newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China Xi'an plane part maker to list A shr.
newsitem.headline: China Xi'an plane part maker to list A shr.

text.p: Xi'an Aircraft International Corporation, Seattle-based U.S. Boeing Co's only plane parts supplier in China, on Tuesday said it would list 54 million A shares on south China's Shenzhen bourse on June 26.

Xi'an Aircraft, based in Xi'an, capital of northwestern China's Shaanxi province, also supplies parts to a number of other leading aircraft makers including Airbus Industrie and Raytheon Co, the Chinese company said in a statement in the Shenzhen-based Securities Times.

Xi'an Aircraft's products include vertical fins and horizontal stabilisers used in Boeing 737-300 and -700 jets, and forward exit doors for Boeing 737-300s, a Xi'an Aircraft official told the Hong Kong-based newsletter, China Securities Bulletin.
Xi'an Aircraft also processes aluminium for construction, which accounted for 54 percent of the company's 1996 sales, the official said.
The company raised net proceeds of 357 million yuan from an initial public offering of 60 million A shares launched earlier this month, the statement said.
It added the firm's staff bought six million A shares, which will be listed six months after the flotation.
The firm's A share prospectus said the company planned to use the stock funds to renovate vertical fin production technology, boost aluminium processing capacity and supplement working capital.
Xi'an Aircraft forecast net profits of 47.35 million yuan for 1997, compared with 39.81 million yuan in 1996 and 37.29 million yuan the previous year, the prospectus said.
Sales were targeted at 475.55 million yuan for this year against 340.67 million yuan in 1996 and 309.47 million yuan in 1995, under Chinese accounting standards.
Sales to Boeing Co accounted for about 35 percent of Xi'an Aircraft's total sales in 1996, the prospectus said.
Xi'an Aircraft has 170 million outstanding shares, composed of 110 million shares held by the state and 60 million A shares restricted to mainland Chinese investors.
